events.title: Sinking of the RMS Lusitania
events.description: The British ocean liner RMS Lusitania was torpedoed by German U-boat U-20 off the southern coast of Ireland and sank in about 18 minutes, killing 1,198 of the nearly 1,960 people aboard, including 128 Americans.
events.significance: The attack intensified anti-German sentiment worldwide and became a key factor in shifting American public opinion, contributing to the United States entering World War I in 1917.

events.title: German Instrument of Surrender Signed at Reims
events.description: General Alfred Jodl, representing the German High Command, signed the unconditional surrender of all German forces at Allied headquarters in Reims, France, to take effect on May 8.
events.significance: This act ended World War II in Europe, leading to the celebration of Victory in Europe (V-E) Day and marking the collapse of Nazi Germany.

events.title: Premiere of Beethoven's Ninth Symphony
events.description: Ludwig van Beethoven's Symphony No. 9 in D minor, featuring the choral 'Ode to Joy' finale, premiered at the Theater am Kärntnertor in Vienna, with the composer, nearly completely deaf, on stage.
events.significance: It was the first major symphony to include vocal soloists and chorus, and it became one of the most celebrated works in Western music; its 'Ode to Joy' theme was later adopted as the anthem of the European Union.

events.title: Birth of Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky
events.description: Russian composer Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky was born in Votkinsk, Russia. He went on to compose works including Swan Lake, The Nutcracker, and the 1812 Overture.
events.significance: Tchaikovsky became one of the most popular and influential composers of the Romantic era, and his ballets and symphonies remain staples of the classical repertoire worldwide.

events.title: Fall of Dien Bien Phu
events.description: After a 56-day siege, Vietnamese Viet Minh forces under General Vo Nguyen Giap overran the French garrison at Dien Bien Phu in northern Vietnam.
events.significance: The decisive defeat ended French colonial rule in Indochina, led to the Geneva Accords and the division of Vietnam, and set the stage for later American involvement in the Vietnam War.
